At that time, Jesus addressed this parable to certain people who relied on themselves as though they were just, and held the rest in contempt: Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee and the second a publican. The Pharisee, standing, prayed these words within himself: O God, I give You thanks that I am not as the rest of mankind, robbers, unjust, adulterers, as this publican also is. I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of everything I possess. And the publican, standing far off, would not even raise his eyes toward heaven, but was beating his breast, saying: O God, be merciful to me, a sinner. I say to you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one; because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.

Brethren: I make known to you the gospel that I proclaimed to you, which you also received, in which you also stand, and through which you also are saved, if you retain it in the form in which I proclaimed it to you, unless it was in vain that you believed. For first of all I handed on to you what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures; that He was buried; that He rose on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures; that He appeared to Cephas, then to the eleven. After that He appeared to more than five hundred brethren together, of whom many remain until now, while some have fallen asleep. Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles; last of all, as to one born before his time, He appeared to me too. For I am the least of the apostles, I who am not worthy to be called an apostle, since I persecuted the Church of God. Yet by God’s grace I am what I am, and within me His grace has not been empty.

At that time, Jesus left the region of Tyre and came by way of Sidon to the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Decapolis. And to Him they bring a man deaf and mute, and they kept begging Him to place His hand upon him. And taking him apart from the crowd, He placed His fingers in his ears; and He spat and touched his tongue; and He looked up to heaven and sighed, and said to him: Ephphetha, which is, Be opened. And at once his ears were opened, and the fetter of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking correctly. And He charged them not to tell anyone. But the more He charged them, so much the more they made it known; and they were all the more amazed, saying: He has done all things well, and He has made the deaf to hear and the mute to speak.

Brethren: We have such confidence toward God through Christ: not that we are sufficient to think anything by ourselves, as if it came from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God, who has also made us qualified ministers of a new covenant, not by the letter but by the spirit; for the letter kills, while the spirit gives life. Now if the ministration of death, formed in letters upon stones, was in glory, so that the sons of Israel could not fix their eyes on the face of Moses because of the glory of his countenance, which is passing away, how will the ministration of the Spirit not be in glory all the more? For if the ministration of condemnation is glory, the ministry of justice abounds much more in glory.

At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Blessed are the eyes that see the things you see. For I say to you that many prophets and kings have desired to see the things you see, yet have not seen them, and to hear the things you hear, yet have not heard them. And behold, a certain lawyer rose up, putting Him to the test and saying: Teacher, what am I to do to possess eternal life? And He said to him: In the law, what is written? How do you read? In answer he said: You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself. And He told him: You have given the right answer; do this, and you will live. But wanting to justify himself, he said to Jesus: And who is my neighbor? And Jesus, taking this up, said: A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell in with robbers, who even stripped him, and having beaten him they went off, leaving him half dead. Now a certain priest happened to be going down that same road; and seeing him, he went by. Likewise a Levite too, being near the spot and seeing him, went on past. But a certain Samaritan, who was on a journey, came up beside him; and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion. And approaching, he bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; and placing him on his own animal, he led him to an inn and looked after him. And on the following day he brought out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said: Look after him; and whatever more you spend, I, when I come back, will repay you. Which of these three, in your view, was neighbor to the man who fell in with the robbers? He replied: The one who showed compassion to him. Then Jesus said to him: Go, and do the same yourself.

Brethren: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. He does not say: And to seeds, as referring to many, but as referring to one: And to your seed, who is Christ. Now this I say: the law, which came into being four hundred and thirty years afterward, does not so annul the testament confirmed by God as to cancel the promise. For if the inheritance comes from the law, then it no longer comes from the promise. But to Abraham God granted it by promise. What, then, is the law? It was laid down because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom He had made the promise, ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator. Now a mediator is not of one; God, however, is one. So is the law against the promises of God? Far from it. For if there had been given a law able to give life, justice would indeed come from the law. But Scripture has confined all things under sin, so that the promise might be granted, from the faith of Jesus Christ, to those who believe.

Then Jesus answered and said: Were not ten cleansed? And the nine, where are they? No one has been found to come back and give glory to God but this foreigner. And He said to him: Arise, go; for your faith has made you whole.

Brethren: Walk in the Spirit, and you will not carry out the desires of the flesh. For the flesh sets its desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these things are set against one another, so that you do not do all that you wish. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are fornication, impurity, immodesty, debauchery, the service of idols, sorceries, enmities, disputes, rivalries, fits of anger, brawls, dissensions, sects, envies, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these; about which I forewarn you, as I have forewarned you, that those who do such things will not gain the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, long-suffering, mildness, faith, modesty, continence, chastity. Against such things there is no law. And those who are Christ’s have crucified their flesh with its vices and lusts.

At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will stand by the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon. For this reason I say to you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the sky: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth far more than they? But which of you, by taking thought, can add one cubit to his stature? And about clothing, why are you anxious? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither labor nor spin. But I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these. Now if God so clothes the grass of the field, which exists today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more you, who are of little faith? Do not be anxious, then, saying: What will we eat, or what will we drink, or with what will we be clothed? For the Gentiles seek after all these things. For your Father knows that you have need of all these things. Seek first, therefore, the kingdom of God and His justice, and all these things will be added to you.

At that time, Jesus was speaking in parables to the chief priests and the Pharisees, saying: The kingdom of heaven has been likened to a king who made a marriage feast for his son. And he sent his servants to call the invited guests to the marriage feast, and they would not come. Once more he sent other servants, saying: Tell the invited guests: Behold, I have prepared my banquet; my bulls and my fattened animals are slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the marriage feast. But they took no notice, and went off, one to his farm and another to his business; while the others laid hold of his servants, treated them outrageously, and put them to death. When the king heard this, he became angry; and he sent his armies and destroyed those murderers, and burned down their city. Then he told his servants: The marriage feast is indeed ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go, then, to the crossroads, and call to the marriage feast whomever you find. And going out into the roads, his servants assembled all they found, the bad and the good; and the marriage feast was filled with those reclining at table. And the king went in to see those at table, and there he saw a man not dressed in a wedding garment. And he asked him: Friend, how did you enter here, not having a wedding garment? But he fell silent. Then the king told the attendants: Bind his hands and feet, and throw him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.

Once more he sent other servants, saying: Tell the invited guests: Behold, I have prepared my banquet; my bulls and my fattened animals are slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the marriage feast. But they took no notice, and went off, one to his farm and another to his business; while the others laid hold of his servants, treated them outrageously, and put them to death. When the king heard this, he became angry; and he sent his armies and destroyed those murderers, and burned down their city. Then he told his servants: The marriage feast is indeed ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go, then, to the crossroads, and call to the marriage feast whomever you find. And going out into the roads, his servants assembled all they found, the bad and the good; and the marriage feast was filled with those reclining at table. And the king went in to see those at table, and there he saw a man not dressed in a wedding garment. And he asked him: Friend, how did you enter here, not having a wedding garment? But he fell silent. Then the king told the attendants: Bind his hands and feet, and throw him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.

Brethren: If we live in the Spirit, let us walk in the Spirit too. Let us not become eager for empty glory, provoking each other, envying each other. Brethren, even if a man is overtaken in some fault, you who are spiritual, instruct someone like this in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you too be tempted. Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ. For if anyone considers himself to be something, when he is nothing, he misleads himself. But let each one examine his own work, and then he will have his glory in himself alone, and not in another. For everyone will carry his own burden. Now let the one who is taught the word share in all good things with the one who teaches him. Do not go astray: God is not mocked. Whatever things a man has sown, these, indeed, he will also reap. For whoever sows in his flesh will also reap corruption from the flesh; but whoever sows in the spirit will reap eternal life from the spirit. And let us not falter in doing good, for in its own time we will reap, provided we do not falter. So then, as long as we have time, let us work what is good toward all, but above all toward those of the household of the faith.

Brethren: I entreat you not to falter in my tribulations for you, which is your glory. On this account I bend my knees before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every fatherhood in the heavens and on earth is named, that He may give you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with might through His Spirit for the inner man, and that Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts; in order that you, rooted and founded in love, may be able to grasp what the breadth and the length and the loftiness and the depth are, together with all the saints, and to know also the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled to the whole fullness of God. And to Him who can do all things far more abundantly than we ask or understand, according to the power that works within us, to Him be glory within the Church and in Christ Jesus, to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

Jesus said to him: You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole mind. This is the greatest and the first commandment. And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hangs the whole law, and the prophets. And when the Pharisees had gathered, Jesus asked them, saying: What is your view concerning the Christ? Whose son is He? They say to Him: David’s. He says to them: How then does David in the spirit call Him Lord, saying: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand, until I make Your enemies the footstool of Your feet? If David, then, calls Him Lord, how is He his son? And no one could answer Him a word, nor from that day did anyone dare to question Him any further.

At that time, getting into a boat, Jesus crossed over and came to His own city. And behold, they were bringing Him a paralytic lying on a bed. And Jesus, when He saw their faith, said to the paralytic: Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven you. And behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves: This man is blaspheming. And when Jesus saw their thoughts, He said: Why do you think evil things in your hearts? Which is easier, to say: Your sins are forgiven you; or to say: Arise and walk? But that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins — then He said to the paralytic: Arise, take up your bed, and go to your house. And he arose and went away to his house. And when the crowds saw it, they were afraid, and they glorified God, who had given such power to men.

At that time, there was a certain ruler whose son was ill at Capernaum. When this man heard that Jesus was coming from Judea into Galilee, he went to Him and was asking Him to come down and heal his son, for he was beginning to die. Then Jesus said to him: Unless you see signs and wonders, you do not believe. The ruler says to Him: Lord, come down before my son dies. Jesus says to him: Go, your son lives. The man believed the word which Jesus had spoken to him, and he was going on his way. And as he was already going down, servants came to meet him and brought word, saying that his son was living. So he was asking them the hour at which he had improved. And they said to him: Yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him. The father then knew that it was that hour in which Jesus had said to him: Your son lives; and he himself believed, and his whole household.

Brethren: Be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of His power. Put on God’s armor, so that you can stand against the devil’s snares. For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the princes and the powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavens. For this reason take up God’s armor, so that you can resist on the evil day, and stand complete in all things. So stand, having your loins girded with truth, and wearing the breastplate of justice, and having your feet shod with the readiness of the gospel of peace; in everything taking the shield of faith, by which you can extinguish all the fiery missiles of the most wicked one. And put on the helmet of salvation, and take the sword of the Spirit, that is, the word of God.

At that time, Jesus told His disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven has been likened to a king who wished to call his servants to account. And when he had begun the reckoning, one was presented to him who owed him ten thousand talents. But since he had nothing with which to repay, his lord ordered that he be sold, and his wife and his children and everything he had, and that repayment be made. But that servant fell down and implored him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything. And the lord of that servant, moved with pity, released him and forgave him the debt. But when that servant had gone out, he found a fellow servant of his who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he was choking him, saying: Pay back what you owe. And his fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything. But he would not; instead he went off and put him in prison until he paid back the debt. Now when his fellow servants saw what was happening, they were deeply grieved, and they came and told their lord all that had taken place. Then his lord called him and said to him: Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Ought not you also, then, to have had pity on your fellow servant, even as I had pity on you? And his lord, being angry, delivered him to the torturers until he repaid the whole debt. So also will My heavenly Father do to you, if you do not forgive, each one his brother, from your hearts.

At that time, the Pharisees withdrew and formed a plan to catch Jesus in His words. And they send their disciples to Him with the Herodians, saying: Teacher, we know that You are truthful and that You teach the way of God in truth, and You are not concerned about anyone; for You do not look upon the person of men. Tell us, then, what You think: is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not? But Jesus, aware of their malice, said: Why are you putting Me to the test, you hypocrites? Show Me the coin used for the tax. And they presented Him with a denarius. And Jesus said to them: Whose image and inscription is this? They say to Him: Caesar’s. Then He says to them: Render, therefore, the things that are Caesar’s to Caesar, and the things that are God’s to God.

Brethren: Be my imitators, and observe those who walk in this way, even as you have our example. For many walk, of whom I often told you, and now tell you even with tears, that they are enemies of the cross of Christ: whose end is perdition, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their disgrace, who set their minds on earthly things. But our way of life is in heaven, from where we also look for the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will reshape the body of our low estate, conformed to the body of His radiance, according to the working by which He is able even to subject all things to Himself. Therefore, my brethren, dearly beloved and most longed for, my joy and my crown, so stand firm in the Lord, dearly beloved. I ask Evodia, and I beseech Syntyche, to think the same thing in the Lord. And I ask you also, true companion: help those women who labored with me in the Gospel, with Clement and the rest of my helpers, whose names are in the book of life.

At that time, while Jesus was speaking to the crowds, behold, a ruler approached and was worshipping Him, saying: Lord, my daughter has just died; but come, lay Your hand on her, and she will live. And Jesus, rising, was following him, and so were His disciples. And behold, a woman who had been suffering from a flow of blood for twelve years approached from behind and touched the hem of His garment. For she was saying within herself: If I touch only His garment, I will be whole. But Jesus, turning and seeing her, said: Take courage, daughter; your faith has made you whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour. And when Jesus had come into the house of the ruler and had seen the flute players and the crowd making an uproar, He was saying: Withdraw; for the girl is not dead, but is asleep. And they were laughing at Him. And when the crowd had been put out, He went in and took her by the hand. And the girl arose. And this report went out into all that land.

At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: When you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place — let the reader understand — then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let him who is on the roof not come down to take anything out of his house; and let him who is in the field not return to take his tunic. But woe to those who are with child and to those who are nursing in those days. And pray that your flight may not be in winter or on the sabbath. For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor will be. And if those days had not been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened. Then if anyone says to you: Behold, here is the Christ, or there, do not believe it. For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will work great signs and wonders, so that even the elect, if possible, would be led into error. Behold, I have foretold it to you. So if they say to you: Behold, He is in the desert, do not go out; Behold, in the inner rooms, do not believe it. For as the lightning comes forth from the east and is seen as far as the west, so also will the coming of the Son of Man be. Wherever the body is, there the eagles also will be gathered together. And immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken; and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; and they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty. And He will send His angels with a trumpet and a loud voice, and they will gather together His elect from the four winds, from the heights of the heavens to their limits. Now learn a parable from the fig tree: when its branch is already tender and the leaves have come out, you know that summer is near. So you also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors. Amen I say to you that this generation will not pass away until all these things come to pass. Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will not pass away.

I, like a vine, have yielded a sweet fragrance, and my blossoms are the fruit of honor and of riches. I am the mother of beautiful love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope. Within me is every grace of the way and the truth; within me, every hope of life and virtue. Come over to me, all you who desire me, and take your fill of what I bring forth. For my spirit is sweet beyond honey, and my inheritance beyond honey and the honeycomb. The remembrance of me is for the generations of the ages. Those who eat me will still hunger, and those who drink me will still thirst. Whoever listens to me will not be brought to shame, and those who work in me will not sin. Those who make me known will have eternal life.
